clue.text: A way to work a Weary Willie

parts.note: MO stands for modus operandi, Latin for a method of working
per means 'a', as in five pounds per head

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get a listless, droopy character moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Weary Willie was a tramp character in British comics, and the name became a byword for a gloomy, lethargic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dejected, listless person who sits around sulking is the sort the old comic name describes.

clue.text: Be "brave"? Tonto's first to flee N American Indian spirit

indicators.note: to flee says this letter runs off, leaving the rest of the phrase

parts.note: to man it out is to bear up bravely, toughing a hard situation out

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word Tonto's is taken

explanation.surface: Tonto, the Lone Ranger's companion, is urged to show courage, yet he is first to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonto is the Lone Ranger's Native American sidekick, which sets the scene; the T that flees is the final one of MAN IT OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Algonquian belief this is the name for a spirit or supernatural power pervading nature.

clue.text: Ordain, say, romance should rise in value

indicators.note: in places the upturned word inside the other

parts.note: to prize something is to value it highly

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a romance is a tale of love or adventure

explanation.surface: A romantic novel is expected to gain in worth, someone decrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should rise' turns TALE upward into ELAT, which goes 'in' PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing a church under government by bishops covers acts such as ordaining clergy, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Force back Scots dancing around piano

indicators.note: around means the dance's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish country dance
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Highland dancers whirl about a piano while shoving it back across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back an attacker or push away an advance is to resist it forcefully.

clue.text: Hotline is buzzing, given Penny and Peg used to row

indicators.note: buzzing suggests a jumbled, excited state, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: The hotline rings off the hook while someone is handed a coin and an oar peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is buzzing' mixes HOTLINE with P.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a peg fixed in the gunwale of a boat, serving as the pivot for an oar while rowing.

clue.text: Guys will become attached to me, "Two-time Maggie"

definitions.text: Guys will become attached to me

parts.note: two written in binary is 10, read as the word ten
Peg and Maggie are both pet forms of Margaret

explanation.surface: A woman nicknamed Two-time Maggie boasts that men will cling to her.
explanation.walkthrough: Guys are the ropes that steady a tent, tied off at ground level; 'Two' is read in binary as 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are tied to this stake driven into the ground, so the clue speaks as the stake itself.

clue.text: Pooped! In motion, scooping nasty bits of tofu up

indicators.note: scooping means the outer word gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad, so it is nasty

indicators.note: in motion means these letters are moving about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Exhausted after scooping up horrible bits of bean curd while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In motion' mixes the letters of 'tofu up', and 'scooping' has OFF hold them between its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooped is slang for exhausted, and being breathless after exertion means just the same.

clue.text: In-form individual in French national team dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter for national is taken out

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, so a side can be called an eleven

explanation.surface: A player in good form for France's national side has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-form' suggests good form; here it means placed in a school form, and the answer is the French word for pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A French pupil is literally someone placed in a school class or form, so the hyphenated wording fits.

clue.text: Half-heartedly went through escalating house checks

indicators.note: through means one piece runs through the middle of the other
escalating means rising, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, British shorthand

indicators.note: half-heartedly means half of the word's heart, one of its two middle letters, is lost

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating, and the past tense of that act is peed

explanation.surface: Someone climbing unenthusiastically through a house, carrying out inspections.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house sharing one wall. 'escalating' turns SEMI up into IMES; 'Half-heartedly' drops one central E of PEED, and PED goes 'through' IMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to hold it back or obstruct it, the verb sense of hinders.

clue.text: End up with radius broken and in support

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: r is the usual abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: Someone finishes up with a fractured arm bone, and in a sling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radius' looks like the arm bone but is its abbreviation; 'broken' mixes it with 'End up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up a structure from below, or lend strength to an argument, is to give it a foundation.

clue.text: To "unfriend" Wally in step #4 of five? That's confused "followership"!

definitions.note: a collective noun standing for the plural set of followers

indicators.note: confused means the collected letters are jumbled together
unfriending means removing a friend, an ally, from the name Wally
#4 of means the fourth letter of the word five is taken

explanation.surface: Social-media advice: drop a foolish friend at the fourth of five steps, and your followers are muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ALLY, a friend, from Wally leaves W; add STEP and E, the fourth letter of five, and 'confused' jumbles them.
explanation.definitionFit: On Twitter, an account's followers were nicknamed by blending tweet with people.

clue.text: For beginners, whole between three and one

definitions.text: For beginners, whole between three and one

indicators.note: between means the first letter of whole sits between the other two
for beginners means only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: w is the beginning of whole, the same 'For beginners' signal applied to it

explanation.surface: A maths lesson for small children: which whole number sits between three and one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'For beginners' takes the first letters of whole, three and one; the W then sits 'between' T and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting down from three to one, the whole number passed in the middle is the one named.

clue.text: Back to pour some ale and wine we've lost

indicators.note: back means the whole string of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a barman pulls a pint of beer from the pump
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Losers drown their sorrows, going back to beer and wine after a heavy defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads PULL + ASTI right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the game is over and no hope is left amounts to admitting defeat.

clue.text: Hard to follow fine heavy metal festival in Cork?

indicators.note: to follow puts the hard letter after the other pieces

parts.note: f stands for fine, as on pencil grades
lead is a heavy metallic element
h stands for hard, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A heavy metal music festival in Ireland comes after a stiff fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is an Irish county and city, and the answer is an Irish festival of music and dance; the '?' flags Cork as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish this word names a festival of traditional music, so one held in Cork is an instance.

clue.text: Suddenly afraid a new King's imminent?

definitions.meaning: cowering, shrinking back in sudden fear
the queen (QU) being sick or unwell suggests a successor king may soon reign

explanation.surface: Courtiers are suddenly afraid, sensing a new king is about to take the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as QU, for queen, plus a word meaning unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing courage and shrinking back in sudden fear is exactly cowering before a threat.

clue.text: With hint of asteism aboard hapless Titanic: "The suspense is killing me!"

indicators.note: aboard means the two letters are taken on board, inside the jumbled ship
hapless, the ship's ill fortune, marks the letters as wrecked and rearranged
a hint of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A witty passenger aboard the doomed liner jokes about the tension.
explanation.walkthrough: Asteism is polite irony or witty mockery. 'hapless' wrecks the ship's name, and 'aboard' takes the two letters in after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of impatient eagerness, said while waiting anxiously for what comes next.

clue.text: Overcast? Presumably overcast if not!

indicators.note: the word is read as 'cast over', the top letter thrown off the front

parts.note: an overcast sky lets no sun through

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's quip: it will surely be cloudy, except when it isn't.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second 'overcast' as 'cast over': the opening S is thrown off. Commenters on the blog disputed this parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce an exception: something happens except on the condition that another thing occurs.

clue.text: 15th Century house found in narrow street, overlooking river

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means sitting above, so the street comes before the river letter
in places the second word inside the first

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or street
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A historic building found in a narrow street with a view over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a royal dynasty, not a building: the red-rose side in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Three kings of the 1400s, Henry IV to Henry VI, came from this royal dynasty.

clue.text: Winding Mediterranean course mostly in very good condition

indicators.note: winding back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
in places the dish inside the other word

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: meze is a selection of small dishes served in Greece, Turkey and the Levant

explanation.surface: A twisting Mediterranean cruise route, most of it in excellent shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MEZE to MEZ, put 'in' ACE to give AMEZCE; 'Winding' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin disorder, marked by itchy inflamed patches, is a medical condition.

clue.text: Where they put e.g. the soup in supermarket song?

definitions.text: Where they put e.g. the soup in supermarket
definitions.meaning: the aisle for tinned goods, read as a can area or zone
an Italian or Provencal lyric set to music

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where the soup aisle is in the supermarket, then breaks into song.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian ballad or lyric poem set to music, akin to a madrigal, is this kind of song.

clue.text: Liking as always to confine female, with force, in it?

indicators.note: to confine means the outer word holds the others inside it

parts.note: aye, also spelt ay, is a poetic word for always
f is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A controlling partner's idea of affection: always keeping a woman shut in, by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; the old Scots and poetic aye, meaning ever, is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural liking or attraction for someone is a fondness, a sense of kinship.

clue.text: Predictably, crossword constructors in America are looking up "aluminum"

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the letters are read upward
in places one word inside the other

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
setters often refer to themselves as us
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, spelt aluminum in the US

explanation.surface: American crossword setters, as expected, are checking the American spelling of a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'us'; 'are looking up' turns the insertion upward before the metal's symbol follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the customary, normal way could have been predicted.

clue.text: Where agreement ended War on Art in Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A peace treaty ends a war on art in the east London suburb of Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a London district. The 1920 Treaty of Trianon, signed at a palace at Versailles, ended the First World War for Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920 treaty concluding the First World War with Hungary was signed at this palace in Versailles.

clue.text: People out of hospital later

indicators.note: out of means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: to people a place is to inhabit it
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: Patients will be discharged from hospital later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to fill a place with inhabitants.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean after a short while, soon, at some time to come.

clue.text: Small scale turning up in buffet-car breakfast

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny weighing device topples over at breakfast in a railway buffet car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small scale' suggests a weighing device or a modest size; it is a botanical scale, and 'turning up' reads TCARB upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this name for a small modified leaf, often scale-like, at the base of a flower.

clue.text: Chemical decomposition of ICI union card

indicators.note: decomposition means breaking down and reforming, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: union abbreviates to U, as in mathematics' set union, and card stays as written

explanation.surface: A chemical breakdown at ICI, the old British chemicals giant, over a union card.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a British chemicals giant; 'decomposition of' mixes ICI, U and CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound, a breakdown product excreted in urine and linked to gout, is a chemical.

clue.text: I arranged for ad in i

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets up an advertisement in the i, a British newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British newspaper; the opening 'I' is the definition, read as the NATO alphabet's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, the code word for the ninth letter is the name of a South Asian country.

clue.text: Is no longer viewed from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: viewed means saw, watched

explanation.surface: Something has vanished, glimpsed only from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of 'to be' describes what used to hold true but has since stopped.

clue.text: Boy busy with a composition

parts.note: a son is a boy child
to be at something is to be busy with it, as in hard at work

explanation.surface: A lad is occupied with a piece of school writing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a musical work for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.

clue.text: Addition of new information — on Tinder profile one hopes it will?

definitions.meaning: bringing records current by adding the latest facts

definitions.text: on Tinder profile one hopes it will?
definitions.meaning: on the dating app one hopes the romance goes up, taking one up in the world

explanation.surface: A note on a dating-app profile, hoping something comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinder is a dating app; the second reading splits the answer into UP and the word for going out with people.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing a record up to date means adding the latest facts, the noun sense of revision.

clue.text: Eighteen in the round — but not doing the nineteenth?

definitions.meaning: a round of golf has eighteen holes, each begun from a tee, so eighteen is the count of tees
the nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, so not drinking there means abstaining

explanation.surface: A golfer plays all eighteen holes but skips the clubhouse bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never drinks alcohol abstains, so skips the bar after a round.

clue.text: A name for cutting edge

indicators.note: cutting means the word for 'for' slices into the other pair

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A title used for a sharp blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts PRO inside A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a theatre stage in front of the curtain, or the paved rim of an airfield, forms an edge.
